candidates.label: Praise of Allah (Hamd)
candidates.definition: The Qur'anic affirmation that praise belongs to Allah, opening al-Fatiha. Related to but not identical with shukr (gratitude); the precise relationship requires scholarly review.

candidates.label: Allah's Lordship of the Worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin)
candidates.normLabel: allah's lordship of the worlds (rabb al-'alamin)
candidates.definition: Allah's lordship over all worlds as affirmed in 1:2. Records the Qur'anic phrase and its immediate context; theological elaboration belongs to tafsir.

candidates.label: The paired divine names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim
candidates.normLabel: the paired divine names ar-rahman and ar-rahim
candidates.definition: The paired divine names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim as they occur together in al-Fatiha (1:1, 1:3). Their pairing and repetition are the extracted phenomenon; interpretation of the distinction belongs to tafsir.

candidates.label: Sovereignty of the Day of Recompense (Malik Yawm ad-Din)
candidates.normLabel: sovereignty of the day of recompense (malik yawm ad-din)
candidates.definition: Allah's sovereignty of the Day of Recompense as stated in 1:4. Distinct from a general hereafter topic: the extracted concept is Allah's ownership/sovereignty of that Day.

candidates.label: Exclusive worship and seeking help (Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in)
candidates.normLabel: exclusive worship and seeking help (iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in)
candidates.definition: The declaration that worship and seeking help are directed to Allah alone (1:5). The classical link to tawhid al-uluhiyyah is noted as related but requires tafsir evidence to assert.

candidates.label: The taught supplication for guidance to the straight path
candidates.normLabel: the taught supplication for guidance to the straight path
candidates.definition: The supplication the Qur'an teaches believers to make: asking Allah for guidance to the straight path (1:6), specified in 1:7 as the path of the favored.

candidates.label: The three groups: favored, anger-earned, astray
candidates.normLabel: the three groups: favored, anger-earned, astray
candidates.definition: The distinction stated in 1:7 between those upon whom Allah bestowed favor, those who earned anger, and those astray. The verse does not name the groups; any identification requires verified tafsir evidence and is not asserted here.

candidates.label: The doubtless Book as guidance
candidates.definition: The opening declaration that the Book is free from doubt and serves as guidance.

candidates.label: Taqwa as condition for receiving guidance
candidates.normLabel: taqwa as condition for receiving guidance
candidates.definition: Taqwa identified in 2:2 as the condition for benefiting from the Book's guidance.

candidates.label: Belief in the unseen (iman bil-ghayb)
candidates.definition: Faith in al-ghayb listed as first quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

candidates.label: Establishing prayer (iqamat as-salah)
candidates.definition: Establishment of salah as second quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

candidates.label: Spending from divine provision (infaq mimma razaqna)
candidates.normLabel: spending from divine provision (infaq mimma razaqna)
candidates.definition: Spending from what Allah provided, third quality of muttaqin in 2:3.

candidates.label: Certainty in the Hereafter (yaqin bil-akhirah)
candidates.definition: Absolute certainty regarding the Hereafter in 2:4.

candidates.label: Success (falah) as outcome of divine guidance
candidates.normLabel: success (falah) as outcome of divine guidance
candidates.definition: State of being muflihun declared in 2:5 for those upon guidance.

candidates.label: Disbelief (kufr) and ineffectiveness of warning
candidates.definition: State in 2:6 where disbelief renders warning equivalent to non-warning.

candidates.label: Sealing of hearts, hearing, and veiling of sight
candidates.normLabel: sealing of hearts, hearing, and veiling of sight
candidates.definition: Divine act in 2:7 of sealing hearts/hearing and veiling sight. Theology deferred.

candidates.label: False profession of faith without possessing it
candidates.normLabel: false profession of faith without possessing it
candidates.definition: Phenomenon in 2:8 of verbal profession without actual belief.

candidates.label: Self-deception (attempting to deceive Allah but deceiving only oneself)
candidates.normLabel: self-deception (attempting to deceive allah but deceiving only oneself)
candidates.definition: Self-deceptive dynamic in 2:9.

candidates.label: Disease in the heart (marad fil-qulub) and its increase
candidates.normLabel: disease in the heart (marad fil-qulub) and its increase
candidates.definition: Spiritual disease in hearts described in 2:10, increased by Allah.

candidates.label: Corruption on earth (fasad fil-ard) and its denial
candidates.normLabel: corruption on earth (fasad fil-ard) and its denial
candidates.definition: Prohibition against corruption (2:11) and false claim of being reformers.

candidates.label: Arrogance toward believers — calling them foolish
candidates.normLabel: arrogance toward believers — calling them foolish
candidates.definition: Arrogance in 2:13 calling believers foolish; divine reversal.

candidates.label: Double-faced conduct — public profession vs. private alliance
candidates.normLabel: double-faced conduct — public profession vs. private alliance
candidates.definition: Dual behavior in 2:14: professing belief publicly, declaring alliance with shayatin privately.

candidates.label: Trading guidance for misguidance — the profitless transaction
candidates.normLabel: trading guidance for misguidance — the profitless transaction
candidates.definition: Commercial metaphor in 2:16 for spiritual exchange.

candidates.label: Parable of the kindled fire — light given then withdrawn
candidates.normLabel: parable of the kindled fire — light given then withdrawn
candidates.definition: First parable in 2:17 comparing hypocrites to one whose fire-light was taken away.

candidates.label: Parable of the rainstorm — darkness, thunder, lightning, fear of death
candidates.normLabel: parable of the rainstorm — darkness, thunder, lightning, fear of death
candidates.definition: Second parable in 2:19-20: rainstorm with darkness, thunder, lightning.

candidates.label: Universal command to worship the Creator
candidates.normLabel: universal command to worship the creator
candidates.definition: First direct address to all mankind in Al-Baqarah commanding worship of the Lord who created them and those before them.

candidates.label: Challenge to produce a surah like the Quran (tahaddi)
candidates.normLabel: challenge to produce a surah like the quran (tahaddi)
candidates.definition: Conditional challenge in 2:23 to produce a single surah matching the revelation, addressed to those in doubt.

candidates.label: Description of Paradise: gardens, rivers, purified spouses, eternal abode
candidates.normLabel: description of paradise: gardens, rivers, purified spouses, eternal abode
candidates.definition: First detailed description of Jannah in Al-Baqarah (2:25): gardens with flowing rivers, fruit provision, purified spouses, eternal dwelling.

candidates.label: Warning of Hellfire: fuel of people and stones, prepared for disbelievers
candidates.normLabel: warning of hellfire: fuel of people and stones, prepared for disbelievers
candidates.definition: First description of Jahannam in Al-Baqarah (2:24): fire fueled by people and stones, specifically prepared for kafireen.

candidates.label: Divine parables (amthal): purpose and divergent reception
candidates.normLabel: divine parables (amthal): purpose and divergent reception
candidates.definition: Allah's willingness to present any parable (even a mosquito) and the bifurcated response: believers recognize truth, disbelievers question intent (2:26).

candidates.label: Covenant-breaking: severing bonds, corruption, and loss
candidates.normLabel: covenant-breaking: severing bonds, corruption, and loss
candidates.definition: Condemnation in 2:27 of those who break Allah's covenant, sever commanded bonds, and spread corruption — declared losers.

candidates.label: Cycle of existence: lifelessness, animation, death, revival, return to Allah
candidates.normLabel: cycle of existence: lifelessness, animation, death, revival, return to allah
candidates.definition: Rhetorical argument in 2:28 tracing human existence through four stages as basis for questioning disbelief.

candidates.label: Human vicegerency (khilafah) on earth
candidates.definition: Divine appointment of a khalifah on earth announced to angels in 2:30, establishing humanity's representative role.

candidates.label: Knowledge (ilm) as distinguishing human capacity
candidates.definition: Teaching Adam all the names (2:31) as demonstration of human epistemic capacity surpassing angels, validated in 2:33.

candidates.label: Repentance (tawbah): Adam receiving words and Allah accepting his return
candidates.normLabel: repentance (tawbah): adam receiving words and allah accepting his return
candidates.definition: Adam receiving kalimat from his Lord and Allah accepting his repentance (2:37), establishing tawbah as divinely enabled recovery.

candidates.label: Address to Children of Israel: remembrance, covenant, exclusive awe
candidates.normLabel: address to children of israel: remembrance, covenant, exclusive awe
candidates.definition: Opening of Bani Israel discourse in 2:40: remember favor, mutual covenant fulfillment, exclusive fear of Allah.

candidates.label: Selling divine signs for a small price
candidates.normLabel: selling divine signs for a small price
candidates.definition: Prohibition in 2:41 against exchanging Allah's ayat for thamanan qaleelan — worldly gain at the cost of spiritual truth.

candidates.label: Mixing truth with falsehood and concealing truth knowingly
candidates.normLabel: mixing truth with falsehood and concealing truth knowingly
candidates.definition: Dual prohibition in 2:42: la talbisoo al-haqqa bil-batil (do not mix) and wa taktumoo al-haqqa (do not conceal) while knowing.

candidates.label: Seeking help through patience and prayer (ista'inoo bis-sabr was-salah)
candidates.normLabel: seeking help through patience and prayer (ista'inoo bis-sabr was-salah)
candidates.definition: Command in 2:45 to seek divine assistance specifically through sabr and salah, noted as difficult except for the khashi'een.

candidates.label: Rescue from Pharaoh and parting of the sea
candidates.normLabel: rescue from pharaoh and parting of the sea
candidates.definition: Sequential reminders in 2:49-50: salvation from Pharaoh's torment, parting the sea, drowning enemies while Bani Israel watched.

candidates.label: Calf worship incident and collective repentance
candidates.normLabel: calf worship incident and collective repentance
candidates.definition: Narrative in 2:51-54: taking calf after Musa's departure, Musa's rebuke, command to repent and kill selves, Allah accepting repentance as at-Tawwab ar-Raheem.

candidates.label: Giving of the Book (Kitab) and Criterion (Furqan) to Musa
candidates.normLabel: giving of the book (kitab) and criterion (furqan) to musa
candidates.definition: Divine bestowal in 2:53 of al-Kitab and al-Furqan to Musa for guidance, establishing dual revelation concept.

candidates.label: Divine provisions in wilderness: clouds, manna, salwa, springs
candidates.normLabel: divine provisions in wilderness: clouds, manna, salwa, springs
candidates.definition: Comprehensive provision narrative across 2:57 and 2:60: cloud shade, manna, salwa, twelve springs from struck stone.

candidates.label: Substituting the commanded word and receiving punishment
candidates.normLabel: substituting the commanded word and receiving punishment
candidates.definition: In 2:58-59: commanded to say 'hittah' but substituted different words, resulting in rijz from the sky for fusuq.

candidates.label: Ingratitude: requesting earthly food over heavenly provision
candidates.normLabel: ingratitude: requesting earthly food over heavenly provision
candidates.definition: In 2:61: complaint about single food type, request for vegetables/garlic/lentils/onions, Musa's rebuke about exchanging adna for khayr.

candidates.label: Humiliation, poverty, and divine anger: cumulative consequences of Bani Israel's transgressions
candidates.normLabel: humiliation, poverty, and divine anger: cumulative consequences of bani israel's transgressions
candidates.definition: Culminating indictment in 2:61: dhilla and maskana stamped, returning with ghadab from Allah, caused by kufr bi-ayat, killing prophets, asiyan, and i'tida'.

candidates.label: Universal salvation criteria: faith in Allah, Last Day, and righteous deeds across communities
candidates.normLabel: universal salvation criteria: faith in allah, last day, and righteous deeds across communities
candidates.definition: In 2:62: believers, Jews, Christians, and Sabians who believe in Allah and the Last Day and do righteous deeds receive reward with no fear or grief — establishing salvation criteria based on faith and action rather than communal identity alone.

candidates.label: Covenant at Mount Sinai: raising the mountain and commanding firm adherence to scripture
candidates.normLabel: covenant at mount sinai: raising the mountain and commanding firm adherence to scripture
candidates.definition: In 2:63: Allah took covenant from Bani Israel, raised Mount Sinai above them, and commanded them to take what was given with strength and remember its contents for taqwa.

candidates.label: Sabbath transgression: transformation into despised apes as deterrent punishment
candidates.normLabel: sabbath transgression: transformation into despised apes as deterrent punishment
candidates.definition: In 2:65-66: those who transgressed the sabbath were told 'be apes, despised' — made as nakal (deterrent) for contemporaries and successors, and mawAAithatan (admonition) for the muttaqeen.

candidates.label: Excessive questioning making divine commands burdensome: the cow narrative
candidates.normLabel: excessive questioning making divine commands burdensome: the cow narrative
candidates.definition: In 2:67-71: Bani Israel asked repeatedly about the cow's attributes despite a simple initial command, making compliance increasingly specific and difficult until they barely managed to fulfill it.

candidates.label: Hardening of hearts (qaswat al-quloob) after witnessing divine signs
candidates.normLabel: hardening of hearts (qaswat al-quloob) after witnessing divine signs
candidates.definition: In 2:74: after witnessing revival through the cow, hearts became hardened like stones or even harder — contrasted with stones that burst forth rivers, split with water, or fall from fear of Allah.

candidates.label: Deliberate distortion (tahreef) of Allah's word after understanding it
candidates.normLabel: deliberate distortion (tahreef) of allah's word after understanding it
candidates.definition: In 2:75: a party among them hears Allah's word, understands it, then deliberately distorts it while knowing — establishing tahreef as conscious post-comprehension alteration.

candidates.label: Writing false scripture with own hands and attributing it to Allah for worldly gain
candidates.normLabel: writing false scripture with own hands and attributing it to allah for worldly gain
candidates.definition: In 2:79: woe to those who write scripture with their own hands then say 'this is from Allah' to exchange it for a small price — double woe for what hands wrote and what they earn.

candidates.label: Believing in part of scripture while disbelieving in part
candidates.normLabel: believing in part of scripture while disbelieving in part
candidates.definition: In 2:85: rhetorical question challenging those who believe in part of al-kitab and disbelieve in part — identified as cause of disgrace in worldly life and severest punishment in Hereafter.

candidates.label: Killing and evicting own people despite covenant prohibition
candidates.normLabel: killing and evicting own people despite covenant prohibition
candidates.definition: In 2:84-85: covenant prohibited shedding blood and eviction, acknowledged while witnessing, yet violated through killing, eviction, cooperation in sin/aggression, and paradoxically ransoming captives whose eviction was forbidden.

candidates.label: Buying worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter
candidates.normLabel: buying worldly life in exchange for the hereafter
candidates.definition: In 2:86: those who bought (ishtaraw) the worldly life for the Hereafter face unlightened punishment and no aid — framing worldly preference as a transactional exchange with eternal consequences.

candidates.label: Envy-driven disbelief: rejecting revelation because Allah bestowed favor on another
candidates.normLabel: envy-driven disbelief: rejecting revelation because allah bestowed favor on another
candidates.definition: In 2:90: Bani Israel sold themselves wretchedly by disbelieving in what Allah revealed out of baghy (outrage/envy) that Allah sends His favor upon whom He wills from among His servants — establishing envy as theological motive for kufr.

candidates.label: Isa ibn Maryam: clear proofs and Holy Spirit support as prophetic credentials
candidates.normLabel: isa ibn maryam: clear proofs and holy spirit support as prophetic credentials
candidates.definition: In 2:87: Allah gave Isa ibn Maryam al-bayyinat and supported him with Ruh al-Qudus — establishing his prophetic credentials parallel to Musa receiving the Kitab.

candidates.label: Systematic rejection pattern: denying some prophets and killing others
candidates.normLabel: systematic rejection pattern: denying some prophets and killing others
candidates.definition: In 2:87 and 2:91: whenever a messenger came with undesired message, Bani Israel were arrogant — denying a party (fareeqan kaththabtum) and killing another party (fareeqan taqtuloona); challenged to explain why they killed prophets before if truly believers.

candidates.label: Verbal compliance masking disobedience: samiAAana wa-AAasayna
candidates.normLabel: verbal compliance masking disobedience: samiaaana wa-aaasayna
candidates.definition: In 2:93: when commanded to take scripture with determination and listen, Bani Israel responded 'samiAAana wa-AAasayna' (we hear and disobey) — and their hearts absorbed calf worship through disbelief.

candidates.label: Greed for life exceeding even polytheists: wishing thousand-year lifespan
candidates.normLabel: greed for life exceeding even polytheists: wishing thousand-year lifespan
candidates.definition: In 2:96: Bani Israel found most greedy for life (ahrasa al-nasi AAala hayat), even more than mushrikeen; one wishes to live a thousand years but longevity cannot remove him from punishment.

candidates.label: Jibril's role: bringing Quran to Prophet's heart confirming previous scripture
candidates.normLabel: jibril's role: bringing quran to prophet's heart confirming previous scripture
candidates.definition: In 2:97: Jibril brought down the Quran upon the Prophet's heart by Allah's permission, confirming (musaddiqan) what was before it, as guidance and glad tidings for believers.

candidates.label: Divine enmity declared against those hostile to Allah, angels, and messengers
candidates.normLabel: divine enmity declared against those hostile to allah, angels, and messengers
candidates.definition: In 2:98: whoever is enemy of Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril, and Mikal — then Allah is enemy to the disbelievers.

candidates.label: Chronic covenant-breaking: every covenant thrown away by a party
candidates.normLabel: chronic covenant-breaking: every covenant thrown away by a party
candidates.definition: In 2:100: every time they made a covenant (AAahadoo AAahdan), a party threw it away (nabathahu); most of them do not believe.

candidates.label: Magic (sihr) narrative: Sulayman exonerated, devils and Harut-Marut trial
candidates.normLabel: magic (sihr) narrative: sulayman exonerated, devils and harut-marut trial
candidates.definition: In 2:102: Bani Israel followed what devils recited during Sulayman's reign; Sulayman did not disbelieve but devils taught sihr including what was sent to Harut and Marut at Babylon who warned they were fitnah; people learned separation magic harming only by Allah's permission; knew purchaser has no Hereafter share.

candidates.label: Throwing scripture behind backs: willful ignorance of known revelation
candidates.normLabel: throwing scripture behind backs: willful ignorance of known revelation
candidates.definition: In 2:101: when messenger confirming what was with them came, a party of People of Book threw Allah's Book behind their backs (waraa thuhoorihim) as if they did not know.

candidates.label: Abrogation (naskh): replacing verses with better or similar
candidates.normLabel: abrogation (naskh): replacing verses with better or similar
candidates.definition: In 2:106: whatever ayah We abrogate (nansakh) or cause to be forgotten, We bring better or similar; establishing divine authority over revelation modification.

candidates.label: Speech etiquette: replacing ambiguous ra'ina with respectful unzurna
candidates.normLabel: speech etiquette: replacing ambiguous ra'ina with respectful unzurna
candidates.definition: In 2:104: believers commanded not to say 'ra'ina' (ambiguous word with disrespectful connotation) but to say 'unzurna' (attend to us) and listen — establishing respectful address to the Prophet.

candidates.label: Post-truth envy: wishing to revert believers after truth became clear
candidates.normLabel: post-truth envy: wishing to revert believers after truth became clear
candidates.definition: In 2:109: many People of Book wish to turn believers back to kufr out of hasad from themselves even after truth became clear to them; believers commanded to pardon and overlook.

candidates.label: Salah and zakah: paired establishment as pillars of devotion
candidates.normLabel: salah and zakah: paired establishment as pillars of devotion
candidates.definition: In 2:110: believers commanded to establish prayer and give zakah together, with assurance that whatever good sent ahead will be found with Allah.

candidates.label: Universal salvation: submitting face to Allah with ihsan
candidates.normLabel: universal salvation: submitting face to allah with ihsan
candidates.definition: In 2:112: whoever submits his face to Allah as muhsin has reward with his Lord; no fear upon them nor grief — establishing universal criterion beyond ethnic/religious identity.

candidates.label: Masjid sanctity: preventing Allah's remembrance as gravest injustice
candidates.normLabel: masjid sanctity: preventing allah's remembrance as gravest injustice
candidates.definition: In 2:114: none more unjust than one who prevents masajid Allah from dhikr of His name and strives for their destruction; they should only enter in fear; disgrace in dunya and great punishment in akhirah.

candidates.label: Refutation of divine sonship: subhanahu and universal qanitoon
candidates.normLabel: refutation of divine sonship: subhanahu and universal qanitoon
candidates.definition: In 2:116: they say Allah took a son; subhanahu! Rather to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth; all are qanitoon to Him — absolute refutation of divine offspring.

candidates.label: Divine origination (BadiAA) and creative command (kun fayakoon)
candidates.normLabel: divine origination (badiaa) and creative command (kun fayakoon)
candidates.definition: In 2:117: Allah is BadiAA (Originator) of heavens and earth; when He decrees a matter He only says 'kun' (Be) and it is (fayakoon) — establishing effortless divine creation without precedent.

candidates.label: Following desires after knowledge: loss of divine protection
candidates.normLabel: following desires after knowledge: loss of divine protection
candidates.definition: In 2:120: if you follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah no protector or helper — warning that knowledge increases accountability.

candidates.label: Judgment Day: no soul suffices for another; no compensation, intercession, or help
candidates.normLabel: judgment day: no soul suffices for another; no compensation, intercession, or help
candidates.definition: In 2:123: fear a Day when no soul suffices for another at all, no compensation accepted, no intercession benefits, no help given — comprehensive description of individual accountability.

candidates.label: Imamah appointment: Ibrahim tested and made leader; covenant excludes wrongdoers
candidates.normLabel: imamah appointment: ibrahim tested and made leader; covenant excludes wrongdoers
candidates.definition: In 2:124: Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with commands and fulfilled them; Allah said 'I will make you imam for people'; Ibrahim asked about descendants; Allah said covenant does not include wrongdoers.

candidates.label: Kaaba construction and purification: Ibrahim and Ismail's joint service
candidates.normLabel: kaaba construction and purification: ibrahim and ismail's joint service
candidates.definition: In 2:125-127: Allah made the House a place of return and security; charged Ibrahim and Ismail to purify it for pilgrims; they raised its foundations praying for acceptance.

candidates.label: Ibrahim's taught supplications: Muslim identity, rites, and future messenger
candidates.normLabel: ibrahim's taught supplications: muslim identity, rites, and future messenger
candidates.definition: In 2:128-129: Ibrahim and Ismail pray to be Muslims, have Muslim descendants, be shown rites, receive repentance, and for a messenger who recites, teaches, and purifies.

candidates.label: Millat Ibrahim: the universal creed excluding sectarian exclusivism
candidates.normLabel: millat ibrahim: the universal creed excluding sectarian exclusivism
candidates.definition: In 2:130-135: turning from millat Ibrahim is self-foolishness; Ibrahim chosen and righteous; submitted to Rabb al-aalameen; willed to descendants; Yaqoob's deathbed tawheed; reject Jewish/Christian exclusivism; follow millat Ibrahim hanifan.

candidates.label: Individual accountability: each nation earns its own; no cross-generational burden
candidates.normLabel: individual accountability: each nation earns its own; no cross-generational burden
candidates.definition: In 2:134 and 2:141: that was an ummah that has passed; it has what it earned and you have what you earned; you will not be asked about what they used to do.

candidates.label: Universal faith declaration: believing in all revelations without distinction
candidates.normLabel: universal faith declaration: believing in all revelations without distinction
candidates.definition: In 2:136: say we believe in Allah and what was revealed to us and to Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqoob, asbaat, Musa, Isa, and all prophets; we make no distinction; we are Muslims to Him.

candidates.label: Sibghat Allah: divine coloring as the best religion
candidates.normLabel: sibghat allah: divine coloring as the best religion
candidates.definition: In 2:138: sibghat Allah — and who is better than Allah in coloring/religion? And we are worshippers of Him.

candidates.label: Qibla change: divine test establishing ummatan wasatan as witnesses
candidates.normLabel: qibla change: divine test establishing ummatan wasatan as witnesses
candidates.definition: In 2:143: thus We made you a middle community to be witnesses over people and Messenger witness over you; previous qiblah was test to distinguish followers from reverters; difficult except for guided; Allah preserves iman.

candidates.label: Mutual remembrance and gratitude: fadhkuroonee adhkurkum wa-ushkuroo lee
candidates.normLabel: mutual remembrance and gratitude: fadhkuroonee adhkurkum wa-ushkuroo lee
candidates.definition: In 2:152: remember Me I will remember you; be grateful to Me and do not deny Me — establishing reciprocal divine-human relationship through dhikr and shukr.

candidates.label: Following desires after knowledge: post-knowledge deviation as zulm
candidates.normLabel: following desires after knowledge: post-knowledge deviation as zulm
candidates.definition: In 2:145: if you follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would then be among the wrongdoers — reiterating that knowledge increases accountability.

candidates.label: Sabr as divine strategy: seeking help through patience and prayer in adversity
candidates.normLabel: sabr as divine strategy: seeking help through patience and prayer in adversity
candidates.definition: In 2:153: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer; indeed Allah is with the patient. In 2:155-157: divine testing through fear, hunger, loss; glad tidings to those who say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un when afflicted; upon them blessings and mercy; they are guided.

candidates.label: Istirja': taught supplication recognizing divine ownership and return in calamity
candidates.normLabel: istirja': taught supplication recognizing divine ownership and return in calamity
candidates.definition: In 2:156: who when disaster strikes them say 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return' — a taught response to calamity affirming divine ownership and ultimate return.

candidates.label: Repentance with reform and clarification: conditions for divine acceptance
candidates.normLabel: repentance with reform and clarification: conditions for divine acceptance
candidates.definition: In 2:160: except those who repent, reform themselves, and make evident what they concealed — those Allah accepts their repentance; He is At-Tawwab Ar-Raheem. Contrasts with 2:159 curse on concealers and 2:161-162 eternal curse on persistent disbelievers.

candidates.label: Cosmic signs in creation: heavens, earth, night/day, ships, rain, creatures, winds, clouds
candidates.normLabel: cosmic signs in creation: heavens, earth, night/day, ships, rain, creatures, winds, clouds
candidates.definition: In 2:164: indeed in creation of heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships sailing with benefit, rain reviving earth, dispersal of creatures, directing winds and controlled clouds are signs for people who reason.

candidates.label: Misplaced love: taking rivals beside Allah and loving them as love of Allah
candidates.normLabel: misplaced love: taking rivals beside allah and loving them as love of allah
candidates.definition: In 2:165: among people are those who take equals besides Allah, loving them as love of Allah; but believers are stronger in love for Allah. If wrongdoers saw punishment they would know all power belongs to Allah.

candidates.label: Halal and tayyib: dual criteria for lawful and wholesome consumption
candidates.normLabel: halal and tayyib: dual criteria for lawful and wholesome consumption
candidates.definition: In 2:168: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth that is lawful (halal) and good (tayyib). In 2:172: O believers, eat from good things We provided and be grateful. In 2:173: specific prohibitions (dead meat, blood, pork, non-divine dedication) with necessity exemption.

candidates.label: Blind ancestral following: rejecting revelation for inherited tradition without understanding
candidates.normLabel: blind ancestral following: rejecting revelation for inherited tradition without understanding
candidates.definition: In 2:170: when told to follow what Allah revealed they say we follow what our fathers did — even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided. Parable in 2:171: disbelievers like one shouting to what hears nothing but calls — deaf, dumb, blind.

candidates.label: Concealment of scripture for worldly gain: eating Fire and divine silence
candidates.normLabel: concealment of scripture for worldly gain: eating fire and divine silence
candidates.definition: In 2:174-176: those who conceal what Allah sent down of the Book and sell it for small price eat only Fire; Allah won't speak to them or purify them on Judgment Day; they exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment; Book sent in truth; dissenters in extreme dissension.

candidates.label: Ayat al-Birr: comprehensive righteousness integrating faith pillars with ethical action
candidates.normLabel: ayat al-birr: comprehensive righteousness integrating faith pillars with ethical action
candidates.definition: In 2:177: righteousness is not turning faces east/west but believing in Allah, Last Day, angels, Book, prophets; giving wealth despite love to relatives, orphans, needy, traveler, askers, freeing slaves; establishing prayer; giving zakah; fulfilling covenants; patience in poverty, hardship, battle. Those are truthful and righteous.

candidates.label: Qisas: legal retribution as life-preserving justice with built-in mercy
candidates.normLabel: qisas: legal retribution as life-preserving justice with built-in mercy
candidates.definition: In 2:178-179: qisas prescribed for murder with proportionality (free for free, slave for slave, female for female); remission by brother should be followed with good conduct; this is alleviation and mercy from your Lord; in qisas there is life O people of understanding so you may attain taqwa.

candidates.label: Fasting (sawm): prescribed for taqwa with exemptions, timing, and fidya provisions
candidates.normLabel: fasting (sawm): prescribed for taqwa with exemptions, timing, and fidya provisions
candidates.definition: In 2:183: O you who believe, fasting is prescribed upon you as upon those before you so you may attain taqwa. In 2:184-185: numbered days; exemptions for sick and travelers with make-up; fidya for those with hardship; Ramadan as month of Quran revelation; Allah intends ease. In 2:187: timing from dawn white thread to nightfall; itikaf restrictions.

candidates.label: Divine nearness: Allah responds to the caller who asks about Him
candidates.normLabel: divine nearness: allah responds to the caller who asks about him
candidates.definition: In 2:186: When My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be rightly guided.

candidates.label: Warfare ethics: proportional engagement, cessation conditions, and fitnah as graver than killing
candidates.normLabel: warfare ethics: proportional engagement, cessation conditions, and fitnah as graver than killing
candidates.definition: In 2:190: Fight in Allah's way those who fight you but do not transgress; Allah does not love transgressors. In 2:191-193: kill where found; fitnah worse than killing; fight until no fitnah and religion is for Allah; if they cease no hostility except against oppressors. In 2:194: sacred month reciprocity; proportional retaliation.

candidates.label: Unjust wealth consumption: prohibition of batil acquisition and bribery of authorities
candidates.normLabel: unjust wealth consumption: prohibition of batil acquisition and bribery of authorities
candidates.definition: In 2:188: Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly (bil-batil) nor offer it as bribery to authorities so that you may knowingly devour a portion of people's wealth in sin.

candidates.label: Ihsan: doing good/excellence as quality beloved to Allah
candidates.normLabel: ihsan: doing good/excellence as quality beloved to allah
candidates.definition: In 2:195: Spend in Allah's way; do not throw yourselves into destruction; and do good — indeed Allah loves the doers of good (al-muhsinin).

candidates.label: Hajj and Umrah: completion, prevention protocols, tamattu', and post-rite remembrance
candidates.normLabel: hajj and umrah: completion, prevention protocols, tamattu', and post-rite remembrance
candidates.definition: In 2:196: Complete hajj and umrah for Allah; prevention requires offering; tamattu'/qiran compensation via sacrifice or fasting. In 2:197-199: taqwa as best provision; no blame seeking bounty; remember Allah at Mash'ar al-Haram acknowledging prior misguidance; hasten from Arafat with istighfar. In 2:200-203: post-rite dhikr exceeding ancestral remembrance.

candidates.label: Dual-world supplication: seeking good in this life and hereafter with protection from Fire
candidates.normLabel: dual-world supplication: seeking good in this life and hereafter with protection from fire
candidates.definition: In 2:201: Among them is one who says: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Contrasted with 2:200: one who asks only for worldly gain with no hereafter share.

candidates.label: Hypocrisy archetype: eloquent speech concealing quarrelsomeness and corruption
candidates.normLabel: hypocrisy archetype: eloquent speech concealing quarrelsomeness and corruption
candidates.definition: In 2:204-206: Among people is one whose speech pleases you in worldly life and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of opponents. When he turns away he strives throughout the land to cause corruption, destroying crops and livestock. Allah does not love corruption. When told to fear Allah, pride seizes him in sin; Hell is sufficient for him.

candidates.label: Entering peace/submission (silm) completely: total commitment to divine order
candidates.normLabel: entering peace/submission (silm) completely: total commitment to divine order
candidates.definition: In 2:208: O you who believe, enter into peace/submission (silm) completely, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed he is to you a clear enemy.

candidates.label: Human unity then disagreement: original community, prophetic arbitration, and envy-driven schism
candidates.normLabel: human unity then disagreement: original community, prophetic arbitration, and envy-driven schism
candidates.definition: In 2:213: Mankind was one community (ummah wahidah) then they disagreed. Allah sent prophets as bearers of glad tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning their differences. Only those who were given the Scripture differed concerning it after clear proofs came to them, out of envy/transgression (baghyan) among themselves. Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed. Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

candidates.label: Spending priorities: hierarchical distribution to parents, relatives, orphans, needy, and travelers
candidates.normLabel: spending priorities: hierarchical distribution to parents, relatives, orphans, needy, and travelers
candidates.definition: In 2:215: They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. And whatever you do of good, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.

candidates.label: Intoxicants and gambling: acknowledged benefit outweighed by greater sin
candidates.normLabel: intoxicants and gambling: acknowledged benefit outweighed by greater sin
candidates.definition: In 2:219: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and [yet some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.

candidates.label: Interfaith marriage prohibition: believing slave preferred over free polytheist
candidates.normLabel: interfaith marriage prohibition: believing slave preferred over free polytheist
candidates.definition: In 2:221: Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. A believing slave woman is better than a polytheist even if she pleases you. Do not marry [women to] polytheistic men until they believe. A believing slave is better than a polytheist even if he pleases you. Those invite to the Fire; Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness.

candidates.label: Divorce legislation: waiting periods, reconciliation rights, khul, and irrevocable divorce procedures
candidates.normLabel: divorce legislation: waiting periods, reconciliation rights, khul, and irrevocable divorce procedures
candidates.definition: In 2:228: Divorced women wait three quru'; husbands have reconciliation priority; reciprocal rights with male darajah. In 2:229: Divorce twice; retain honorably or release graciously; khul ransom when fearing hudud failure. In 2:230: Third divorce requires intervening marriage. In 2:231-232: No harm-retention; no preventing remarriage.

candidates.label: Breastfeeding legislation: two-year period, paternal provision, capacity principle, and mutual weaning consent
candidates.normLabel: breastfeeding legislation: two-year period, paternal provision, capacity principle, and mutual weaning consent
candidates.definition: In 2:233: Mothers breastfeed two complete years for whoever wishes completion. Upon the father is their provision and clothing bil-ma'ruf. No soul burdened beyond capacity. No mother harmed through child nor father through child. Weaning by mutual consent and consultation. Wet-nursing permitted with fair payment.

candidates.label: Oaths: unintentional (laghw) exemption with heart-intention accountability
candidates.normLabel: oaths: unintentional (laghw) exemption with heart-intention accountability
candidates.definition: In 2:224-225: Do not make Allah an excuse through oaths against righteousness, piety, and peacemaking. Allah does not hold you accountable for laghw in your oaths but holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned. Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.

candidates.label: Widow provisions: four-month-ten-day iddah, one-year bequest, and autonomous remarriage
candidates.normLabel: widow provisions: four-month-ten-day iddah, one-year bequest, and autonomous remarriage
candidates.definition: In 2:234: Widows wait four months and ten days; no blame for acceptable self-conduct after term. In 2:235: Indirect proposals permitted; secret commitments prohibited. In 2:240: Bequest of one year maintenance without expulsion; voluntary departure permitted.

candidates.label: Middle prayer (salat al-wusta): specific maintenance command with devout standing
candidates.normLabel: middle prayer (salat al-wusta): specific maintenance command with devout standing
candidates.definition: In 2:238: Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer (salat al-wusta), and stand before Allah devoutly obedient (qanitin).

candidates.label: Good loan to Allah (qard hasan): charitable spending with manifold divine multiplication
candidates.normLabel: good loan to allah (qard hasan): charitable spending with manifold divine multiplication
candidates.definition: In 2:245: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And Allah withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.

candidates.label: Cosmic balance (daf' Allah): divine checking of people through others prevents earth corruption
candidates.normLabel: cosmic balance (daf' allah): divine checking of people through others prevents earth corruption
candidates.definition: In 2:251: If it were not for Allah checking [some] people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.

candidates.label: No compulsion in religion: religious freedom established as divine principle
candidates.normLabel: no compulsion in religion: religious freedom established as divine principle
candidates.definition: In 2:256: There shall be no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

candidates.label: Ayat al-Kursi: comprehensive declaration of divine sovereignty, knowledge, and transcendence
candidates.normLabel: ayat al-kursi: comprehensive declaration of divine sovereignty, knowledge, and transcendence
candidates.definition: In 2:255: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

candidates.label: Divine wilayah: Allah brings believers from darkness to light; taghut leads disbelievers from light to darkness
candidates.normLabel: divine wilayah: allah brings believers from darkness to light; taghut leads disbelievers from light to darkness
candidates.definition: In 2:257: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve - their allies are Taghut. They take them out of the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.

candidates.label: Charity ethics: kind word superior to harmful giving; quality standards; sincerity vs show-off
candidates.normLabel: charity ethics: kind word superior to harmful giving; quality standards; sincerity vs show-off
candidates.definition: In 2:263: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. In 2:264: Do not render vain your charities with reproach and injury. In 2:267: Spend from the good things you have earned. In 2:268: Satan promises poverty; Allah promises forgiveness and bounty.

candidates.label: Riba prohibition: explicit trade-riba distinction with divine war declaration for persistence
candidates.normLabel: riba prohibition: explicit trade-riba distinction with divine war declaration for persistence
candidates.definition: In 2:275: Those who consume riba will not stand except as one whom shaytan has driven to madness. That is because they say trade is like riba. But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden riba. Whoever receives admonition from his Lord and desists may keep his past gains. But whoever returns to it - those are companions of the Fire. In 2:279: If you do not desist, be informed of war from Allah and His Messenger.

candidates.label: Debtor relief: mandatory respite for hardship cases; forgiveness as superior charitable act
candidates.normLabel: debtor relief: mandatory respite for hardship cases; forgiveness as superior charitable act
candidates.definition: In 2:280: And if someone is in hardship, then [let there be] postponement until [a time of] ease. But if you give [from your right as] charity, then it is better for you, if you only knew.

candidates.label: Contract documentation: written debt records, impartial scribes, witness requirements, and justice rationale
candidates.normLabel: contract documentation: written debt records, impartial scribes, witness requirements, and justice rationale
candidates.definition: In 2:282: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write [it] between you in justice... And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses... And do not be [too] weary to write it, whether it is small or large, for its [specified] term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and closer to preventing doubt between you, except when it is an immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves.

candidates.label: Closing creedal affirmation: unified belief in Allah, angels, revealed books, and all messengers without distinction
candidates.normLabel: closing creedal affirmation: unified belief in allah, angels, revealed books, and all messengers without distinction
candidates.definition: In 2:285: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.' And they say, 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination.'

candidates.label: Capacity principle: Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity
candidates.normLabel: capacity principle: allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity
candidates.definition: In 2:286: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned.

candidates.label: Closing supplication: divine pardon sought for forgetfulness, error, and excessive burdens
candidates.normLabel: closing supplication: divine pardon sought for forgetfulness, error, and excessive burdens
candidates.definition: In 2:286: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.

candidates.label: Quranic hermeneutics: muhkamat (precise) and mutashabihat (ambiguous) verses with interpretive boundaries
candidates.normLabel: quranic hermeneutics: muhkamat (precise) and mutashabihat (ambiguous) verses with interpretive boundaries
candidates.definition: In 3:7: It is He who sent down the Book; in it are precise verses (muhkamat) — they are the foundation of the Book — and others ambiguous (mutashabihat). Those with deviation in hearts follow the ambiguous seeking discord and interpretation. Only Allah knows its interpretation. Those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it; all is from our Lord.

candidates.label: Heart deviation (zaygh): spiritual pathology driving pursuit of ambiguous texts for discord
candidates.normLabel: heart deviation (zaygh): spiritual pathology driving pursuit of ambiguous texts for discord
candidates.definition: In 3:7: Those in whose hearts is deviation (zaygh) follow the ambiguous from it, seeking discord (fitnah) and seeking its interpretation. In 3:8: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us.

candidates.label: Divine self-witness of tawheed: Allah, angels, and people of knowledge testify to divine unity and justice
candidates.normLabel: divine self-witness of tawheed: allah, angels, and people of knowledge testify to divine unity and justice
candidates.definition: In 3:18: Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge — maintaining justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

candidates.label: Worldly desires taxonomy: seven categories of material attraction contrasted with eternal reward
candidates.normLabel: worldly desires taxonomy: seven categories of material attraction contrasted with eternal reward
candidates.definition: In 3:14: Beautified for people is love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up gold and silver, fine branded horses, cattle, and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return. In 3:15: For the muttaqin: gardens with rivers, eternal abode, purified spouses, divine approval.

candidates.label: Five virtues taxonomy: patience, truthfulness, obedience, spending, and pre-dawn forgiveness-seeking
candidates.normLabel: five virtues taxonomy: patience, truthfulness, obedience, spending, and pre-dawn forgiveness-seeking
candidates.definition: In 3:17: The patient, the truthful, the obedient, those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn.

candidates.label: Prophet-killing and justice-enforcer persecution: triple crime with total deed nullification
candidates.normLabel: prophet-killing and justice-enforcer persecution: triple crime with total deed nullification
candidates.definition: In 3:21: Those who disbelieve in Allah's signs and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among people — give them tidings of painful punishment. In 3:22: Their deeds are voided in this world and the Hereafter; no helpers for them.

candidates.label: False religious security: 'Fire only numbered days' doctrine identified as fabrication-based delusion
candidates.normLabel: false religious security: 'fire only numbered days' doctrine identified as fabrication-based delusion
candidates.definition: In 3:24: That is because they say 'Never will the Fire touch us except for numbered days,' and they were deluded in their religion by what they were fabricating.

candidates.label: Divine sovereignty (Malik al-Mulk): comprehensive supplication acknowledging absolute divine control over dominion, honor, provision, and cosmic cycles
candidates.normLabel: divine sovereignty (malik al-mulk): comprehensive supplication acknowledging absolute divine control over dominion, honor, provision, and cosmic cycles
candidates.definition: In 3:26: Say, O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will; You honor and humble; in Your hand is all good; You are over all things competent. In 3:27: You cause night to enter day and day into night; bring living from dead and dead from living; provide without measure.

candidates.label: Love-following reciprocity: loving Allah requires following the Prophet, resulting in divine love and forgiveness
candidates.normLabel: love-following reciprocity: loving allah requires following the prophet, resulting in divine love and forgiveness
candidates.definition: In 3:31: Say, If you love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

candidates.label: Divine election of families: Adam, Noah, Abraham's family, and Imran's family chosen above all worlds
candidates.normLabel: divine election of families: adam, noah, abraham's family, and imran's family chosen above all worlds
candidates.definition: In 3:33: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds. In 3:34: Descendants, some of them from others. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

candidates.label: Maryam's election and purification: chosen, purified, and preferred above all women of the worlds
candidates.normLabel: maryam's election and purification: chosen, purified, and preferred above all women of the worlds
candidates.definition: In 3:42: And when the angels said, O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. In 3:43: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow.

candidates.label: Zakariyya's supplication for righteous offspring and angelic announcement of Yahya
candidates.normLabel: zakariyya's supplication for righteous offspring and angelic announcement of yahya
candidates.definition: In 3:38: Thereupon Zakariyya called upon his Lord: My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication. In 3:39: The angels called him while he stood praying in the chamber: Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a Word from Allah, honorable, abstaining, a prophet from the righteous.

candidates.label: Isa's miracles: four signs performed by divine permission establishing prophetic authority
candidates.normLabel: isa's miracles: four signs performed by divine permission establishing prophetic authority
candidates.definition: In 3:49: Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I create for you from clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission; I heal the blind and the leper and give life to the dead by Allah's permission; I inform you of what you eat and store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you if you are believers.

candidates.label: Virgin birth of Isa: kun fayakoon creative fiat paralleling divine creation without paternal cause
candidates.normLabel: virgin birth of isa: kun fayakoon creative fiat paralleling divine creation without paternal cause
candidates.definition: In 3:47: She said, My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me? He said, Thus is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it 'Be' and it is.

candidates.label: Isa's legislative authority: confirming prior Torah while making lawful some previously forbidden things
candidates.normLabel: isa's legislative authority: confirming prior torah while making lawful some previously forbidden things
candidates.definition: In 3:50: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.

candidates.label: Hawariyyun's testimony: disciples declare faith, Islam, and request inscription among witnesses
candidates.normLabel: hawariyyun's testimony: disciples declare faith, islam, and request inscription among witnesses
candidates.definition: In 3:52: The disciples said, We are supporters of Allah; we have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims. In 3:53: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses.

candidates.label: Isa-Adam creation parallel: both created by divine fiat without paternal cause as argument against deification
candidates.normLabel: isa-adam creation parallel: both created by divine fiat without paternal cause as argument against deification
candidates.definition: In 3:59: Indeed, the example of Jesus before Allah is like the example of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was.

candidates.label: Mubahalah: mutual invocation of divine curse upon liars as ultimate truth-establishment mechanism
candidates.normLabel: mubahalah: mutual invocation of divine curse upon liars as ultimate truth-establishment mechanism
candidates.definition: In 3:61: Then whoever argues with you about it after knowledge has come to you, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars.

candidates.label: Kalimat sawa': equitable common word as foundation for interfaith dialogue with People of the Book
candidates.normLabel: kalimat sawa': equitable common word as foundation for interfaith dialogue with people of the book
candidates.definition: In 3:64: Say, O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah, not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords instead of Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.

candidates.label: Millat Ibrahim: Abraham as hanif Muslim, neither Jew nor Christian, defining primordial monotheism
candidates.normLabel: millat ibrahim: abraham as hanif muslim, neither jew nor christian, defining primordial monotheism
candidates.definition: In 3:67: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim. And he was not of the polytheists. In 3:68: Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him and this prophet and those who believe. And Allah is the ally of the believers.

candidates.label: Truth-concealment and talbis: mixing haqq with batil as deliberate deception strategy
candidates.normLabel: truth-concealment and talbis: mixing haqq with batil as deliberate deception strategy
candidates.definition: In 3:71: O People of the Scripture, why do you confuse the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know. In 3:78: And indeed, there is among them a party who alter the Scripture with their tongues so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. And they say, This is from Allah, but it is not from Allah. And they speak untruth about Allah while they know.

candidates.label: Covenant-selling: exchanging Allah's covenant and oaths for small price resulting in total eschatological deprivation
candidates.normLabel: covenant-selling: exchanging allah's covenant and oaths for small price resulting in total eschatological deprivation
candidates.definition: In 3:77: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them; and they will have a painful punishment.

candidates.label: Mithaq al-nabiyyin: universal covenant binding all prophets to believe in and support the confirming messenger
candidates.normLabel: mithaq al-nabiyyin: universal covenant binding all prophets to believe in and support the confirming messenger
candidates.definition: In 3:81: And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, saying, Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him. He said, Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My commitment? They said, We have acknowledged it. He said, Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.

candidates.label: Repentance theology: acceptance for reformers, closure for escalating disbelievers, futility of material ransom at death
candidates.normLabel: repentance theology: acceptance for reformers, closure for escalating disbelievers, futility of material ransom at death
candidates.definition: In 3:89: Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves. For indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. In 3:90: Indeed, those who reject the message after their belief and then increase in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray. In 3:91: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never would the capacity of the earth in gold be accepted from one of them.

candidates.label: True righteousness (birr): unattainable without spending from beloved possessions as measure of sincere devotion
candidates.normLabel: true righteousness (birr): unattainable without spending from beloved possessions as measure of sincere devotion
candidates.definition: In 3:92: Never will you attain the good reward until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.

candidates.label: Ka'bah at Bakkah: first house established for mankind, blessed, guidance for worlds, containing clear signs and sanctuary security
candidates.normLabel: ka'bah at bakkah: first house established for mankind, blessed, guidance for worlds, containing clear signs and sanctuary security
candidates.definition: In 3:96: Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Makkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In 3:97: In it are clear signs such as the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe.

candidates.label: Hajj obligation: pilgrimage to the House as universal duty upon mankind conditional on finding a way (istita'ah)
candidates.normLabel: hajj obligation: pilgrimage to the house as universal duty upon mankind conditional on finding a way (istita'ah)
candidates.definition: In 3:97: And due to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.

candidates.label: Habl Allah: collective adherence to Allah's rope as antidote to division, remembering divine favor of transformed enmity
candidates.normLabel: habl allah: collective adherence to allah's rope as antidote to division, remembering divine favor of transformed enmity
candidates.definition: In 3:103: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it.

candidates.label: Amr bi-ma'ruf wa nahy an munkar: enjoining right and forbidding wrong as defining characteristic of the best nation
candidates.normLabel: amr bi-ma'ruf wa nahy an munkar: enjoining right and forbidding wrong as defining characteristic of the best nation
candidates.definition: In 3:104: And let there be arising from you a nation inviting to all that is good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those will be the successful. In 3:110: You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah.

candidates.label: Khayra ummah: Muslim community declared best nation produced for mankind based on moral activism and faith
candidates.normLabel: khayra ummah: muslim community declared best nation produced for mankind based on moral activism and faith
candidates.definition: In 3:110: You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.

candidates.label: Dual-rope exception: abasement lifted only through covenant from Allah and covenant from people
candidates.normLabel: dual-rope exception: abasement lifted only through covenant from allah and covenant from people
candidates.definition: In 3:112: They have been put under humiliation wherever they are overtaken, except for a covenant from Allah and a rope from the Muslims. And they have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah and have been put under destitution.

candidates.label: Ummah qaimah: upright community among People of the Book practicing night devotion, amr/nahy, and hastening to good
candidates.normLabel: ummah qaimah: upright community among people of the book practicing night devotion, amr/nahy, and hastening to good
candidates.definition: In 3:113-114: They are not all the same; among the People of the Scripture is a community standing in obedience, reciting the verses of Allah during periods of the night and prostrating. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous.

candidates.label: Frost-wind parable: worldly spending without faith likened to frost-laden wind destroying harvest of self-wrongers
candidates.normLabel: frost-wind parable: worldly spending without faith likened to frost-laden wind destroying harvest of self-wrongers
candidates.definition: In 3:117: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like that of a wind containing frost which strikes the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys it. And Allah has not wronged them, but they wrong themselves.

candidates.label: Bitanah prohibition: forbidding intimate alliances with those outside the faith who actively seek Muslim corruption
candidates.normLabel: bitanah prohibition: forbidding intimate alliances with those outside the faith who actively seek muslim corruption
candidates.definition: In 3:118: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare you any ruin. They wish you would have hardship. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater.

candidates.label: Anger restraint: kazimin al-ghayth and pardoning people as defining ethical traits of the muttaqin
candidates.normLabel: anger restraint: kazimin al-ghayth and pardoning people as defining ethical traits of the muttaqin
candidates.definition: In 3:134: Who spend during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good.

candidates.label: Riba prohibition: explicit ban on consuming interest doubled and multiplied with taqwa-success linkage
candidates.normLabel: riba prohibition: explicit ban on consuming interest doubled and multiplied with taqwa-success linkage
candidates.definition: In 3:130: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah that you may be successful.

candidates.label: Post-sin repentance pattern: remembering Allah, seeking forgiveness, and not persisting knowingly after moral failure
candidates.normLabel: post-sin repentance pattern: remembering allah, seeking forgiveness, and not persisting knowingly after moral failure
candidates.definition: In 3:135: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and do not persist in what they have done while they know.

candidates.label: Angelic reinforcement: divine military aid through descending angels escalating from 3000 to 5000 conditional on sabr and taqwa
candidates.normLabel: angelic reinforcement: divine military aid through descending angels escalating from 3000 to 5000 conditional on sabr and taqwa
candidates.definition: In 3:124-125: Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you remain patient and conscious of Allah and the enemy come upon you in rage, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels having marks of distinction.

candidates.label: Alternating days: divine rotation of fortune and misfortune among people as test mechanism to distinguish believers and select martyrs
candidates.normLabel: alternating days: divine rotation of fortune and misfortune among people as test mechanism to distinguish believers and select martyrs
candidates.definition: In 3:140: If a wound should touch you - there has already touched the opposing people a wound similar to it. And these days We alternate among the people so that Allah may make evident those who believe and may take to Himself from among you martyrs.

candidates.label: Rabbana supplication: taught prayer combining forgiveness for sins/excesses, request for firm footing, and victory over disbelievers
candidates.normLabel: rabbana supplication: taught prayer combining forgiveness for sins/excesses, request for firm footing, and victory over disbelievers
candidates.definition: In 3:147: And their words were not but that they said, Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess committed in our affairs and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.

candidates.label: Jahiliyyah thought: pre-Islamic fatalistic assumptions resurfacing in believers under battlefield crisis
candidates.normLabel: jahiliyyah thought: pre-islamic fatalistic assumptions resurfacing in believers under battlefield crisis
candidates.definition: In 3:154: Then there came upon you after the distress security — drowsiness covering a party of you, while another party had become anxious about themselves, thinking wrongly about Allah with the assumption of jahiliyyah.

candidates.label: Divine pardon after failure: Allah's 'afw toward believers despite battlefield disobedience and weakness
candidates.normLabel: divine pardon after failure: allah's 'afw toward believers despite battlefield disobedience and weakness
candidates.definition: In 3:152: Until when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you back from them in order to test you. And He has already pardoned you. And Allah is the Possessor of Bounty for the believers.

candidates.label: Counterfactual grief prohibition: divine making of hasrah (regret) in hearts through 'what if' thinking about the dead
candidates.normLabel: counterfactual grief prohibition: divine making of hasrah (regret) in hearts through 'what if' thinking about the dead
candidates.definition: In 3:156: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers who traveled through the land or were fighting, 'If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed,' so that Allah makes that a source of regret in their hearts.

candidates.label: Scripture commodification: selling divine revelation for trivial worldly gain as wretched purchase
candidates.normLabel: scripture commodification: selling divine revelation for trivial worldly gain as wretched purchase
candidates.definition: In 3:187: And when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, 'You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it.' But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.

candidates.label: Mata' al-ghurur: worldly life definitively characterized as enjoyment of delusion
candidates.normLabel: mata' al-ghurur: worldly life definitively characterized as enjoyment of delusion
candidates.definition: In 3:185: And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion.

candidates.label: Hypocrite proximity to kufr: verbal profession of faith disconnected from heart conviction as closer to disbelief
candidates.normLabel: hypocrite proximity to kufr: verbal profession of faith disconnected from heart conviction as closer to disbelief
candidates.definition: In 3:167: And that He might make evident those who are hypocrites. For it was said to them, 'Come, fight in the way of Allah or defend.' They said, 'If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you.' They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah is most Knowing of what they conceal.

candidates.label: Quadruple imperative closing: isbiruu/sabiroo/rabitoo/ittaqoo as comprehensive endurance formula for believers
candidates.normLabel: quadruple imperative closing: isbiruu/sabiroo/rabitoo/ittaqoo as comprehensive endurance formula for believers
candidates.definition: In 3:200: O you who have believed, be patient and endure and guard the frontiers and fear Allah that you may be successful.

candidates.label: Blasphemous poverty claim: 'Allah is poor we are rich' as divinely recorded transgression warranting burning punishment
candidates.normLabel: blasphemous poverty claim: 'allah is poor we are rich' as divinely recorded transgression warranting burning punishment
candidates.definition: In 3:181: Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, while we are rich.' We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right and will say, 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.'

candidates.label: Ulu al-albab dhikr-tafakkur profile: fourfold remembrance posture combined with creation reflection yielding theological insight
candidates.normLabel: ulu al-albab dhikr-tafakkur profile: fourfold remembrance posture combined with creation reflection yielding theological insight
candidates.definition: In 3:190–191: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding, who remember Allah while standing or sitting or on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, saying, 'Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You; protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'

candidates.label: Salvation formula: distance from Fire combined with Jannah admission as the definition of true success (fawz)
candidates.normLabel: salvation formula: distance from fire combined with jannah admission as the definition of true success (fawz)
candidates.definition: In 3:185: So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success.

candidates.label: Single origin of humanity: creation from one soul and its mate as basis for taqwa and kinship obligations
candidates.normLabel: single origin of humanity: creation from one soul and its mate as basis for taqwa and kinship obligations
candidates.definition: In 4:1: O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah through whom you ask one another and the wombs.

candidates.label: Orphan wealth guardianship: prohibition of consumption, requirement of testing maturity, and witnessed handover
candidates.normLabel: orphan wealth guardianship: prohibition of consumption, requirement of testing maturity, and witnessed handover
candidates.definition: In 4:2,5-6: Give orphans their properties, do not substitute bad for good, do not consume their properties into yours. Do not give weak-minded your property. Test orphans until marriageable age; if sound judgement perceived, hand over their wealth with witnesses.

candidates.label: Fractional inheritance legislation: precise shares for children, parents, spouses, and siblings as hudud Allah
candidates.normLabel: fractional inheritance legislation: precise shares for children, parents, spouses, and siblings as hudud allah
candidates.definition: In 4:11-12: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male what is equal to share of two females... These are hudud Allah. Detailed fractions: half, quarter, eighth, two-thirds, third, sixth for various heirs after bequests and debts.

candidates.label: Women's inheritance right: explicit guarantee of obligatory share for women alongside men regardless of estate size
candidates.normLabel: women's inheritance right: explicit guarantee of obligatory share for women alongside men regardless of estate size
candidates.definition: In 4:7: For men is a share of what parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much - an obligatory share (naseeban mafroodan).

candidates.label: Repentance conditions: accepted for ignorant sin followed by prompt reform, rejected for deathbed or persistent disbelief
candidates.normLabel: repentance conditions: accepted for ignorant sin followed by prompt reform, rejected for deathbed or persistent disbelief
candidates.definition: In 4:17-18: The repentance accepted by Allah is only for those who do wrong in ignorance then repent soon after. But repentance is not accepted of those who do evil until death comes and one says 'I repent now,' nor of those who die as disbelievers.

candidates.label: Solemn marriage covenant: mithaq ghaleeth as inviolable bond prohibiting reclamation of mahr upon divorce
candidates.normLabel: solemn marriage covenant: mithaq ghaleeth as inviolable bond prohibiting reclamation of mahr upon divorce
candidates.definition: In 4:21: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant (mithaqan ghaleethan)?

candidates.label: Maharim categories: comprehensive list of permanently prohibited marriage relations by blood, nursing, and marriage
candidates.normLabel: maharim categories: comprehensive list of permanently prohibited marriage relations by blood, nursing, and marriage
candidates.definition: In 4:23: Prohibited to you are your mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brother's daughters, sister's daughters, milk-mothers, milk-sisters, wives' mothers, step-daughters under guardianship, sons' wives, and two sisters simultaneously.

candidates.label: Trade by mutual consent: tijarah an taradin as the only permissible basis for wealth exchange among believers
candidates.normLabel: trade by mutual consent: tijarah an taradin as the only permissible basis for wealth exchange among believers
candidates.definition: In 4:29: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only in lawful business by mutual consent from you. And do not kill yourselves.

candidates.label: Kaba'ir and sayyi'at: avoiding major sins causes expiation of minor sins and grants noble entry
